PROCLAMATION NO. 174/2013
A PROCLAMATION TO ESTABLISH THE LAND TRANSPORT
AUTHORITY
WHEREAS, the establishment of a reliable, comprehensive, adequate efficient
and safe land transport system is decisive for the socio-economic growth of
our country;
WHEREAS, the appropriate utilization of a land transport system is dependent
upon the setting up and regulation of adequate standards and technical
methods; and
WHEREAS, it is necessary to take into account the experience acquired of the
restrictive role played by the dual accountability of the zoba branch offices on
the efficient and effective implementation of the duties and functions of the
land transport;
NOW, THEREFORE, it is proclaimed as follows:
PART ONE
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1. Short Title
This Proclamation may be cited as "The Land Transport Authority
Establishment Proclamation No 174/2013."
Article 2. Definitions
In this Proclamation, unless the context otherwise requires:
(1)"Authority" means the Land Transport Authority established pursuant
to Article 4 of this Proclamation;

(2)"Bicycle" means a vehicle propelled by the motive power of the person
operating the same;
(3)"Carriage" means any vehicle drawn or pushed by person or drawn by
animal;
(4)"Commercial Land Transport" means Public and/or Private land
transport commercial service and hence:
(a) "Public commercial land transport" shall mean any transport
service provided for the carrying of passengers or goods by any
person, for hire or remuneration;
(b)Private commercial land transport shall mean any transport
service provided for carrying employees and goods necessary
and complimentary for own business use only;
(5) "Director General" means the Director General of the Authority
appointed under the provisions of this Proclamation and mandated to
oversee the land transport affairs of the State of Eritrea.
(6) "Land Transport" shall include road transport, rail transport and
telpher.
(7)"Minister" or "Ministry" means the Minister or Ministry of Transport
and Communications, respectively;
(8)) "Motor vehicle" means a vehicle propelled by mechanical or
electrical power, such as a truck, motorcycle, motorcar, public service
vehicle, tractor, special mobile equipment, train and telpher;
(9)"Passenger" means any person riding in a vehicle, other than the driver,
conductor or any other person assigned to work on a vehicle;
(10) "Person" means any natural or juridical person engaged in land
transport;

(11) "Regulatory Documents" means all permits and certificates
issued by the Authority;
(12) "Road" means any road, highway or any other travel route
including a bridge, which is customarily used by vehicles, other than
private road not open to all traffic;
(13) "Special Mobile Equipment" means any vehicle designed,
adapted or used for agriculture, horticulture, livestock raising, road
construction, building, digging or any other similar operation;
(14) "Train" means a vehicle constructed or adapted for use and used
primarily for travel on rails of a railway line;
(15) "Telpher" means a vehicle used to transport passengers and
goods using cable way;
(16) "Vehicle" means any type of wheeled vehicle classified as
motorized and non motorized vehicles; which shall comprise carriage,
bicycle, motor vehicle, trailer, semi-trailer, train and telpher; and
(17) A word imparting a masculine gender shall include the feminine
as well.
Article 3. Scope of Application of the Proclamation
(1)This Proclamation shall apply to all vehicles that use road, railway and
cable way and to all matters relating to land transport.
(2)This Proclamation may not apply to military vehicles registered under
the Ministry of Defence for military use only.

PART TWO
THE LAND TRANSPORT AUTHORITY
Article 4. Establishment of the Land Transport Authority
(1) The Land Transport Authority (hereinafter referred to as the "Authority")
is hereby established as an autonomous public authority having its own
juridical personality.
(2) The Authority shall be accountable to the Minister.
The Authority shall have its head office in Asmara and may as deemed
necessary establish branch offices at in different parts of Eritrea.
Article 6. Objectives of the Authority
The objectives of the Authority shall be the following:
(1) the establishment and development of an overall integrated national
land transport system and the planning as well as the regulation of the
use, maintenance, expansions management of the roads, railways and
cable ways within Eritrea;
(2) the provision and enhancement of reliable, safe, economical,
efficient, comfortable, sustainable and equitably distributed land
transport service;
(3) establishing and regulating a high standard of safety and
infrastructural facilities for land transport service and ensuring safe
traffic movements; and
(4) exerting all efforts for the reduction of environmental pollution
attributable to land transport.

Article 7. Powers, Duties, Responsibilities and Functions of the Authority
(1)The Authority is the sole government body vested with the regulatory
powers to:
(a) prepare draft regulations pertaining to the administration and
attainment of the objectives of this proclamation and submit the
same for the Minister's approval and action;
(b) supervise and control the utilization of land transport services as
well as issuing of regulations and regulatory documents, including
renewal, revocation or transfer of permits, approval of vehicles
and equipment of the land transport sector;
(c) exercise and implement all necessary and appropriate measures for
the effective realization of the objectives of this Proclamation;
(d) represent the Ministry in all its dealings with third parties with
respect to land transport activities;
(e) delegate, with the prior approval of the Minister, part of its
powers and duties to zonal and sub-zonal administrations or
municipalities or other government bodies provided that they
shall, in exercising the powers and duties so delegated to them

standards issued by the Authority; and
(t) Develop the overall institutional capacity of the land transport sub
sector.
(2) The Authority shall, among others, have the following duties and

Article 8. Organs of the Authority

Article 9. Management of the Authority

Article 11. Budget
The Authority's budget shall be allocated by the Government.
Article 12. Books of Accounts and Annual Reports
(1)The Authority shall keep complete and accurate accounts of its
expenditures and revenues and shall within four (4) months after the
expiry of each fiscal year submit duly audited statement of expenditures
and revenues to the Minister.
(2) The books of account and all financial matters of the Authority shall be

PART THREE
MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS
Article 13. Use of Regulatory Document
(1) No regulatory documents, including permits, may be transferred
and/or assigned to another person without the approval of the
Authority.
(2) A regulatory document shall be valid for such period as may be
specified therein and may be renewed.
Article 14. Inspection and control
(1) The Authority shall monitor that all land transport standards and
requirements laid down in this Proclamation are complied with.
(2) The Authority may, as part of its monitoring functions, carry out
random tests and initiate measurements and control measures. Such
monitoring activities may be carried out without prior notice.
(3) The Authority may order the owner or owner's representative to
be present during the inspection and to submit all necessary
documents to the Authority.
(4) The Authority may order the establishment of internal control
system to ensure that the requirement laid down in this
Proclamation are complied with. Documents showing the compliance
of the requirements as regards internal control shall also be prepared.
Article 15. Exclusive Rights and Contracts
(1) The Authority may, where it finds it necessary, grant to
persons, enterprises or associations engaged in Pllblic
commercial land transport exclusive or restricted franchises so

as to:
(a) encourage investors to engage in the provision of public
commercial land transport service to localities where there
is no such service or where it is inadequate; or
(b) support the efforts of the people of certain localities in
constructing and maintaining roads with their own labour and
at their own expenses.
(2) Without prejudice to sub-Article (1) of this Article, nothing herein
contained shall be deemed to prohibit or restrict the right of such
transporter to conclude exclusive contracts of cargo with any person
engaged in public commercial land transport.
Article 16. Exemption from Payment
The Minister may, on the basis of reciprocity and in consultation with the
concerned Government bodies, grant exemption to diplomatic and
consular missions and other foreign and international mISSIOns and
organizations from the payment of fees to be levied on the registration of
vehicles and the issuance of driving licenses.
Article 17. Duty to Provide Information
(1) The Authority may, directly or through appropriate government
agencies, request information necessary for the implementation of this
Proclamation. The information so requested shall be delivered in writing
within a stipulated deadline. Where the deadline is not complied with,
one of the penalties enumerated under Article 18(1) hereof may be
applicable to any permit, approval or other certificate issued pursuant to
this Proclamation.

(2) The Authority may, directly or through appropriate government
agencies, request information necessary for tasks which are transferred
to the Authority in connection with international agreements ratified by
the Government of the state of Eritrea.
Article 18. Civil Sanctions
(1) Where a person fails to comply with requirements laid down in this
Proclamation or in regulatory documents, the Authority may take one
or more of the following measures:
(a) give an order to the person to comply with the requirements
within a stipulated deadline;
(b) impose of a fine not exceeding ten thousand (10,000) Nakfa;
(c) reduce the period of validity of the regulatory document;
(d) suspend the regulatory document; or
(e) revoke the regulatory document.
(2) In addition to the circumstances described in sub-Article (1) of this
Article, the regulatory document may be revoked if the person to
whom the document is issued:
(a) agrees in writing with the Authority that the document should be
revoked;
(b)enters into liquidation or bankruptcy; or
(c) terminates his business activities.
Article 19. Judicial Review
(1) Any person aggrieved by an adverse decision of the Director
General of the Authority pursuant to this Proclamation may
seek a review by the Minister within thirty (30) days of such a

decision.
(2) Where the person is not satisfied by a decision of the Minister
such person may further seek a review by the High Court of
Eritrea within thirty days (30) of the Minster's decision. The
High Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction to hear and decide
the case.
(3) The High Court shall set aside a decision of the Minister ifit
finds to be:
(a) arbitrary, an abuse of discretion or otherwise inconsistent
with the law;
(b) not consistent with required procedures; or
(c) unsupported by substantial evidence ..
(4) The decision of the High court shall be final.
Article 20. Criminal Penalties
Any person who violates the provisions of this Proclamation or regulations
issued hereunder shall be punished in accordance with the Penal Code of
Eritrea.
Article 21. Power to Issue Regulations
The Minister may, for the effective realization of the objectives of this
proclamation, issue regulations pursuant to this Proclamation.
Article 22. Repeals and Savings
(1) Any provisions of law or directive concerning matters provided for
in this Proclamation are hereby repealed and replaced by this
Proclamation.

(2) All Regulations and Directives issued under the Land Transport
Proclamation No. 111/2000 shall be deemed to have been issued
under this Proclamation and shall continue in force.
Article 23. Effective Date
This Proclamation shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the
Gazette of Eritrean Laws.
